VERIDANE - INTERNAL - Product Safety Committee memo PSC-2026-07
Date: 2 Oct 2026     From: Elena Kowalczyk, VP Quality & Product Safety     To: Executive Leadership Team

Subject: GV-400 series combination gas valve - voluntary recall (CPSC Fast Track)

Summary
- Affected units: ~41,200 GV-400/GV-410 combination gas valves, date codes 2507-2612, sold to OEMs for commercial rooftop units and unit heaters.
- Issue: diaphragm seat can deform under sustained high-inlet-pressure conditions, allowing gas to pass when the valve is commanded closed. 17 field reports of gas odor; 2 reports of delayed ignition causing cabinet damage; no injuries reported.
- Root cause: change of diaphragm compound supplier (Q1 2025); supplier lot material out of spec on compression set. Corrective action complete; replacement valves shipping from Mequon plant since 28 Sep.
- Regulatory: CPSC Fast Track filed 22 Sep; joint recall notice expected the week of 19 Oct. Canada (Health Canada) notification filed.
- Cost: reserve booked in Q3 $21.6M (field replacement, OEM labour reimbursement, logistics). Range $18-26M. Supplier recovery claim of ~$9M lodged, not recognised.
- Customer impact: three OEMs (incl. our 2nd-largest BCV customer) have paused new GV-400 orders pending the recall notice. Included in updated guidance.

# Veridane Fluid Technologies, Inc. (NASDAQ: VRDF)
## Q3 FY2026 Letter to Shareholders — quarter ended 30 September 2026

**DRAFT v1 for CFO / VP-IR review — not for distribution. Quiet period in effect until release (Thursday 5 November 2026, 4:05 pm ET).**

Dear Fellow Shareholders,

Data-center demand is powering Veridane's growth. Total backlog ended the quarter at $918.0 million, up 13.0% year over year, and Thermal & Data Center Solutions backlog rose 22.0% to a record $574.2 million, including two new hyperscale awards won during the quarter. TDC net sales grew 13.4%. Total net sales were $412.6 million, down 6.0% year over year, as data-center strength was more than offset by a softer commercial HVAC and gas-valve market and by the voluntary GV-400 recall we filed with the CPSC in September. Adjusted EBITDA was $48.7 million, an 11.8% margin, and adjusted EPS was $0.15. GAAP results, including the $21.6 million recall charge and $6.2 million of restructuring charges, are shown in the KPI table accompanying this letter.

The story of the quarter is a company moving fast on two fronts: capturing the largest growth opportunity in our market while dealing quickly and directly with a product issue in our valves business. We believe both were handled the way Veridane should handle them, and both are reflected in the numbers that follow.

**Highlights**

- Record TDC backlog of $574.2 million, up 22.0% year over year; total backlog $918.0 million, up 13.0%.
- Two new hyperscale data-center awards won in the quarter.
- TDC net sales up 13.4% to $156.3 million.
- Adjusted EBITDA of $48.7 million, an 11.8% margin; adjusted EPS of $0.15.
- Voluntary, proactive GV-400 recall filed with the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission under its Fast Track program; root cause identified and corrected, replacement valves shipping since 28 September.
- Project Keystone launched, targeting $35 million of annualized run-rate cost savings by the end of Q2 FY2027.

**Segment review**

*Thermal & Data Center Solutions.* Net sales were $156.3 million, up 13.4% from $137.8 million a year ago, driven by hyperscale and colocation customers. Our CR-9 rear-door heat exchanger is ramping with the two hyperscale customers announced in Q2, and we won two further hyperscale awards during the quarter. Demand for liquid cooling continues to broaden beyond early adopters, and our engineering teams are qualifying additional product configurations with several customers. Segment backlog reached a record $574.2 million, up 22.0%, giving us multi-quarter visibility on volumes and mix. We are managing component lead times, plant scheduling and installation timelines closely so that this backlog converts to revenue on time and at the quality level these customers expect.

*Building Controls & Valves.* Net sales were $256.3 million, down 14.9% from $301.2 million, reflecting continued softness in commercial construction and lower gas-valve volumes. In September we filed a voluntary recall of approximately 41,200 GV-400 and GV-410 combination gas valves with the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission under its Fast Track program, after our quality team identified that a diaphragm component could allow gas to pass when the valve is commanded closed. This was a proactive, customer-first action. We identified the root cause — a supplier lot out of specification — completed corrective action, and began shipping replacement valves from our Mequon plant on 28 September. No injuries have been reported. We recorded a $21.6 million charge in the quarter to cover field replacement, OEM labor reimbursement and logistics. Three OEM customers, including our second-largest BCV customer, have paused new GV-400 orders pending the recall notice; that pause is reflected in the outlook below. Underlying demand in commercial HVAC remains subdued, and we are competing on service and delivery rather than price.

**Outlook**

Our priorities for the fourth quarter are executing the recall to completion, converting TDC backlog into revenue, and delivering the first savings from Project Keystone. Keystone targets $35 million of annualized run-rate savings by the end of Q2 FY2027, spanning procurement, manufacturing footprint and overhead, and we took a $6.2 million restructuring charge in the quarter to put that program in motion. Savings begin contributing as the program phases in, and the data-center backlog gives us the volume base to realize them.

Reflecting lower BCV volumes, the recall, and the OEM order pauses, we are updating our FY2026 outlook. We now expect net sales of $1.66-1.70 billion, compared with $1.78-1.84 billion previously, and adjusted EBITDA of $205-215 million, compared with $255-270 million previously. Free cash flow was an outflow of $11.3 million in the quarter; we are holding capital spending to essential projects, prioritizing the projects that serve data-center demand, and managing inventory and receivables tightly.

As of September 30, 2026, we were not in compliance with the financial maintenance covenants under our credit agreement. We have requested a waiver and amendment from our lenders and are in active discussions with the bank group. We ended the quarter with $96.4 million of cash. Further detail will be included in our Form 10-Q.

**Closing**

The third quarter tested this company, and our people responded the way we want Veridane to respond: quickly, openly and with the customer first. Our quality team found the issue, we filed with the CPSC under its Fast Track program, and replacement valves were shipping before the quarter closed. That same urgency is now applied to cost and cash through Project Keystone. The strategic picture is unchanged — thermal management for data centers is the fastest-growing part of our market, our backlog is at a record, and we intend to convert it. To our 6,200 employees, thank you for the pace and care you brought to the recall and to our customers this quarter.

We appreciate your continued trust and your investment in Veridane.

Dana Whitcombe, President & Chief Executive Officer
Mark Ostrander, EVP & Chief Financial Officer

**Forward-looking statements:** This letter contains forward-looking statements within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995, including statements regarding our outlook, backlog conversion, cost-savings programs, recall remediation, liquidity, and lender discussions. Words such as "expect," "target," "intend," "plan" and similar expressions identify these statements. Actual results may differ materially from those expressed or implied, including as a result of the matters described above and of the risks described in "Risk Factors" in our Annual Report on Form 10-K filed with the SEC, and in our Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026. We undertake no obligation to update these statements except as required by law.

## Q3 FY2026 Letter to Shareholders — quarter ended 30 September 2026

**DRAFT v1 for CFO / VP-IR review — not for distribution. Quiet period in effect until release (Thursday 5 November 2026, 4:05 pm ET).**

Dear Fellow Shareholders,

Data-center demand is powering Veridane's growth. Total backlog ended the quarter at $918.0 million, up 13.0% year over year, and Thermal & Data Center Solutions backlog rose 22.0% to a record $574.2 million, including two new hyperscale awards won during the quarter. TDC net sales grew 13.4%. Total net sales were $412.6 million, down 6.0% year over year, as data-center strength was more than offset by a softer commercial HVAC and gas-valve market and by the voluntary GV-400 recall we filed with the CPSC in September. Adjusted EBITDA was $48.7 million, an 11.8% margin, and adjusted EPS was $0.15. GAAP results, including the $21.6 million recall charge and $6.2 million of restructuring charges, are shown in the KPI table accompanying this letter.

The story of the quarter is a company moving fast on two fronts: capturing the largest growth opportunity in our market while dealing quickly and directly with a product issue in our valves business. We believe both were handled the way Veridane should handle them, and both are reflected in the numbers that follow.

**Highlights**

- Record TDC backlog of $574.2 million, up 22.0% year over year; total backlog $918.0 million, up 13.0%.
- Two new hyperscale data-center awards won in the quarter.
- TDC net sales up 13.4% to $156.3 million.
- Adjusted EBITDA of $48.7 million, an 11.8% margin; adjusted EPS of $0.15.
- Voluntary, proactive GV-400 recall filed with the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission under its Fast Track program; root cause identified and corrected, replacement valves shipping since 28 September.
- Project Keystone launched, targeting $35 million of annualized run-rate cost savings by the end of Q2 FY2027.

**Segment review**

*Thermal & Data Center Solutions.* Net sales were $156.3 million, up 13.4% from $137.8 million a year ago, driven by hyperscale and colocation customers. Our CR-9 rear-door heat exchanger is ramping with the two hyperscale customers announced in Q2, and we won two further hyperscale awards during the quarter. Demand for liquid cooling continues to broaden beyond early adopters, and our engineering teams are qualifying additional product configurations with several customers. Segment backlog reached a record $574.2 million, up 22.0%, giving us multi-quarter visibility on volumes and mix. We are managing component lead times, plant scheduling and installation timelines closely so that this backlog converts to revenue on time and at the quality level these customers expect.

*Building Controls & Valves.* Net sales were $256.3 million, down 14.9% from $301.2 million, reflecting continued softness in commercial construction and lower gas-valve volumes. In September we filed a voluntary recall of approximately 41,200 GV-400 and GV-410 combination gas valves with the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission under its Fast Track program, after our quality team identified that a diaphragm component could allow gas to pass when the valve is commanded closed. This was a proactive, customer-first action. We identified the root cause — a supplier lot out of specification — completed corrective action, and began shipping replacement valves from our Mequon plant on 28 September. No injuries have been reported. We recorded a $21.6 million charge in the quarter to cover field replacement, OEM labor reimbursement and logistics. Three OEM customers, including our second-largest BCV customer, have paused new GV-400 orders pending the recall notice; that pause is reflected in the outlook below. Underlying demand in commercial HVAC remains subdued, and we are competing on service and delivery rather than price.

**Outlook**

Our priorities for the fourth quarter are executing the recall to completion, converting TDC backlog into revenue, and delivering the first savings from Project Keystone. Keystone targets $35 million of annualized run-rate savings by the end of Q2 FY2027, spanning procurement, manufacturing footprint and overhead, and we took a $6.2 million restructuring charge in the quarter to put that program in motion. Savings begin contributing as the program phases in, and the data-center backlog gives us the volume base to realize them.

Reflecting lower BCV volumes, the recall, and the OEM order pauses, we are updating our FY2026 outlook. We now expect net sales of $1.66-1.70 billion, compared with $1.78-1.84 billion previously, and adjusted EBITDA of $205-215 million, compared with $255-270 million previously. Free cash flow was an outflow of $11.3 million in the quarter; we are holding capital spending to essential projects, prioritizing the projects that serve data-center demand, and managing inventory and receivables tightly.

As of September 30, 2026, we were not in compliance with the financial maintenance covenants under our credit agreement. We have requested a waiver and amendment from our lenders and are in active discussions with the bank group. We ended the quarter with $96.4 million of cash. Further detail will be included in our Form 10-Q.

**Closing**

The third quarter tested this company, and our people responded the way we want Veridane to respond: quickly, openly and with the customer first. Our quality team found the issue, we filed with the CPSC under its Fast Track program, and replacement valves were shipping before the quarter closed. That same urgency is now applied to cost and cash through Project Keystone. The strategic picture is unchanged — thermal management for data centers is the fastest-growing part of our market, our backlog is at a record, and we intend to convert it. To our 6,200 employees, thank you for the pace and care you brought to the recall and to our customers this quarter.

We appreciate your continued trust and your investment in Veridane.

Dana Whitcombe, President & Chief Executive Officer
Mark Ostrander, EVP & Chief Financial Officer
